entries.final_answer: Six kitty-specs/ walkers still decide 'is this a Mission?' for themselves instead of using the shared read-side predicate is_selectable_mission_dir: doctor topology (_collect_topology_rows), _coordination_doctor._resolve_mission_dirs, _review_cycle_reconcile_doctor._mission_dirs_for, materialize._mission_dirs_to_process, charter_activate._collect_inflight_missions and release.changelog.build_changelog_block. Residue folders (no meta.json, or an untracked id-less meta.json) are therefore listed, scanned or processed as Missions, and each walker's local rule can drift from the one authority (#6758, follow-up to #5875).
entries.question: What problem does this Mission solve?

entries.final_answer: Every one of the six walkers decides per child through is_selectable_mission_dir (one git probe per walk at most), so a residue folder never appears as a Mission in any of them; doctor topology no longer prints residue rows with 'meta.json not found'; each changed walker has a test with a residue child and a selectable Mission that would fail on a walker-local rule; and an architectural gate fails if any of the six loses the predicate call.
entries.question: How will we know this Mission is successful?

entries.final_answer: Out of scope: the audit engine's deliberately looser is_mission_dir population (src/specify_cli/audit/engine.py, #6757 owns it); any new residue reporting surface (doctor identity keeps that role); the predicate's own rule and the write-seam is_kitty_specs_residue call sites that already route through it; and walkers outside the six the issue names.
